title: Ridgeway Retail opportunity log
content:
Quick field notes + outreach plan for Ridgeway Retail (mid-market chain, ~120 stores).

Account snapshot:
- HQ: Austin, TX. Public job postings for head of data + cloud infra (hiring ramp).
- Tech stack: AWS-heavy (EKS, RDS), using Snowflake for analytics per public job posting.
- Current AI/R&D signals: RFP issued Q4 2025 for conversational store assistant (omnichannel). Mentioned interest in on-prem for PCI-sensitive flows.
- Primary use-case we can sell: cashier-assist + customer chat triage + returns triage (reduce agent TTR).
- Estimated ARR profile: mid-market retailer, likely pilot < $100k but enterprise if adoption (scale across org).

Why Redwood could win (hypotheses):
- They care about predictable latency during peak retail hours (holiday sales). Redwood's routing + dedicated options are strong sell.
- Data sensitivity: they'd prefer VPC/private deployment for POS integration. Redwood Private + KMS will be a differentiator vs hosted-only vendors.
- Cost focus: they pilot many features; showing unit economics via Redwood Optimize (batching / cache) reduces friction.

Key contacts (prospect map, to confirm on discovery):
- Dir. Digital Experience: Jordan Martinez (likely champion) — LinkedIn shows focus on customer journeys.
- Head of Infra/Cloud: Ravi Anand — cares about VPC, region residency, HSM/KMS.
- Product Manager (conversational): Emily Chong — buyer for conversational assistant pilots.
- Legal/Security: Natasha Green — will gate any on-prem or private deployments.

Signals & red flags:
- + Signal: They mentioned 'fast response during checkout' in RFP — latency SLO will be a top priority.
- + Signal: Multi-cloud cost controls in job description aligns with Redwood Optimize messaging.
- - Red flag: Procurement historically pushes for lowest TCO; need clear pilots to prove ROI.
- - Red flag: Heavy vendor evaluation committee; long procurement cycles.

Discovery questions (openers for intro call):
- What are the top three customer-facing NL/LLM features you're hoping to ship in the next 6 months?
- How do you currently route AI requests (hosted vendor vs on-prem)? Any compliance constraints we should know about?
- What latency / uptime targets are non-negotiable (e.g., <150ms 95th p50 during sale windows)?
- Who will own the integration and who are the stakeholders for infra / security approvals?

Outbound sequence (recommended 6-touch, personalized):
1) Email 1 (Intro): 1-sentence value prop (latency + private deployments), 1 line social proof (retailer X decreased returns triage time 30%). CTA: 15-min intro.
2) LinkedIn note + add: reference RFP 'conversational store assistant' + quick stat.
3) Email 2 (tech note): short snippet on VPC/on-prem packaging + 1-pager link. Call out KMS/region residency.
4) Call attempt + voicemail: mention holiday traffic latency guarantee + offer architecture workshop.
5) Email 3 (pilot offer): propose 6-week pilot scope, success metrics (reduce agent handle time by 20%, <200ms p95), price anchor (estimate $XXk).
6) Executive touch: short note from Head of Partnerships with a customer case study.

Suggested subject lines / snippets:
- Subject A: "15 min? Low-latency conversational pilots for Ridgeway stores"
- Subject B (sec): "VPC + KMS pilot for POS-sensitive prompts"
- Opening line: "Saw your RFP for a conversational assistant — quick idea that keeps card data on your network and halves agent TLDR time."

Pilot scope (6 weeks recommended):
- Week 0: kickoff + access (API keys, test accounts), security questionnaire start.
- Week 1–2: integration w/ demo dataset (returns transcripts), baseline metrics.
- Week 3–4: tune prompts + model variant A/B, latency and cost reporting in Console.
- Week 5–6: run shadow traffic in 10 stores, collect NPS/training metrics, deliver playbook + rollback plan.
- Pilot success criteria (mutually agreed): 
  - p95 latency < 250ms for customer-facing flows
  - 15–25% reduction in agent triage time
  - Cost per handled conversation < defined threshold (TBD)

Objection handling matrix (quick):
- "We can't host outside our network / data leaves our systems": signal to move to Redwood Private + start security pack; loop in Natasha Green and infra early.
- "Pricing too high for pilot": propose capped pilot fee + win-back credits if enterprise contract signs. Highlight Optimize-led cost savings projections.
- "We already have vendor X": ask what gaps vendor X shows (latency, SLOs, quantization/cost), propose 2-week latency proof-of-concept.
- "Procurement long / multiple approvals": map stakeholders; propose separate technical workshop for infra/security to speed approvals.

Pricing anchor thoughts (preparation):
- Pilot price: recommend $35k–65k fixed depending on integration complexity (POS connectors, PII redaction). Keep number flexible.
- Enterprise conversion: tiered reserved capacity estimate — need to run rough TCO model once we have message volume. Use Redwood Optimize to produce delta vs hosted competitor.

Collateral to attach / prepare before outreach:
- One-pager: "Redwood Private for Retail" (focus on VPC, KMS, audit logs) — link to internal Confluence (CONFLUENCE-OPS-4821).
- Short case study: Retailer Y holiday latency win (anonymized).
- Architecture diagram: sample POS integration + private control plane (one-slide).

Internal asks / next steps:
- Liam: can you draft pilot SOW template for retail POS connectors? (Due EOD Wed)
- Priya: connect me with security SME for NatGreen pre-reads (intro by Fri).
- Sales SDR: prioritize Jordan Martinez contact; attempt call Tues/Thu 9–11am CT.

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep emails short — retail buyers prefer concise, outcome-driven asks.
- If they push for cost, pull Optimize calc early and show per-conversation delta.
- Avoid long platform feature lists on first outreach. Lead with the business metric (reduce agent time / faster checkout).

Open questions to resolve before next touch:
- What is their expected monthly request volume for pilot? (need to price)
- Confirm whether their POS vendor supports outbound webhooks or only batch syncs.
- Who owns audit logs retention policy? Legal tag required?

Timestamps / interactions log (to fill as we go):
- 2026-01-17: Initial scrape + RFP PDF downloaded.
- 2026-01-20: Email to Jordan (sent).
- 2026-01-23: LI add to Jordan (pending).
- 2026-02-02: Reply from Emily Chong — requested architecture workshop (schedule).
- 2026-02-05: Workshop scheduled for 2026-02-12 (invite pending).

End-of-file checklist before pilot SOW:
- Security summary + evidence of KMS/HSM integration ready
- Pilot SOW template + estimate ranges
- 1-pager + 2-slide architecture ready for workshop

-- Maya
